edbDesc: An attractive force that occurs when an electric potential is applied across the boundary between a metallic surface and the surface of a semiconducting material. The magnitude of the force depends on the voltage and the specific materials involved.
title: Johnsen-Rahbek effect
description: Put a voltage between a metal plate and a slightly conductive stone or ceramic touching it, and the two cling far harder than ordinary static would allow, because charge piles up across the tiny gaps where they touch. Danish engineers Alfred Johnsen and Knud Rahbek reported it in 1923 and built relays and loudspeakers on it.
effect: a voltage makes a metal and a semiconducting surface cling tightly together
usedIn: Electrostatic chucks holding silicon wafers in chip fabs
strength: A few hundred volts gives a grip of a few kilopascals, enough to hold a wafer flat, many times the pull of plain static at that voltage.
pickWhy: Specific, named effect doing a real job (wafer chucks); not in the deck. Discovered around 1917, published 1923.
